meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen saw a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so start with who decided that.
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
"The zero stands." On what basis, and was Owen heard before you entered it, because procedure 4.1 says you speak with him first. Answer that, or I'm walking from here to the principal's office.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft all the time, Hale, that's what an outline is for. Show me the line, and show me the October 15 outline with the date on it. I'm writing both down.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed in today's meeting. I still expect the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me or heard from Owen, and a copy of both the line you say is not in Hamlet and his dated October 15 outline. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see the line and the dated outline for herself; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because the meeting ended before the evidence was put in front of her.
What moved her: Naming a specific misquoted line and a dated outline whose argument the essay drops got her asking a real question and writing things down, because both are tied to Owen's own work and she can check them herself.
What cost ground: Opening by refusing to talk and declaring the zero final with no reason given, because it confirmed her belief that the school decides first and explains later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; nothing Hale raised touched late nights or the night before the due date, so the evidence never came near that moment; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with one sentence owning that the zero went in before you called her, then put the play and the October 15 outline on the desk and let her check the line herself before she has to ask.
